summary:
North Chungcheong stands under the national framework of South Korea. The province has no separate law on gender identity or gender expression; the national provisions on criminalisation, legal gender recognition, marriage and anti-discrimination apply here as they do elsewhere in the country.

The province's documented trans-specific event is the death of Byun Hui-su, a 23-year-old transgender woman and the country's first transgender soldier, found dead at her home in Cheongju on 3 March 2021. A counsellor raised the alarm after 28 February. She had been discharged over gender-affirming surgery, and her challenge to that discharge had been rejected in July 2020. The death became the reference point for national debate on the treatment of transgender service members.

Public grief and demands for LGBT protections followed the death. The National Human Rights Commission honoured her, and prosecutors and activists called for an anti-discrimination bill, its eighth introduction since 2007; the June 2020 draft had included gender-identity provisions. A society-wide discourse of responsibility followed. No new provincial law resulted from the incident.
tangentialFactors:
No further trans-specific incidents in North Chungcheong appear in the available sources. Documented enforcement, litigation and violence connected to transgender people in South Korea are concentrated in other parts of the country; the province's documented trans-specific record consists of the 2021 death in Cheongju and the national protection pressure it generated.

Because no provincial law was enacted in response, any protection a trans visitor or resident relies on in North Chungcheong is national in origin rather than provincial.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of North Chungcheong hold no provincial-level protection. The province has not enacted law in response to the 2021 death in Cheongju, and legal gender recognition, partnership recognition and anti-discrimination remedies available to residents are national in origin.

The National Human Rights Commission's recognition of Byun Hui-su and the renewed calls for an anti-discrimination bill that followed her death were national processes; no provincial legislative response is documented.
outOfScopeNotes:
No provincial breakdown exists for the national survey data on transgender discrimination, and the sources reviewed record no North Chungcheong-specific figures on enforcement, healthcare access, school facilities or violence.

The province's documented trans-specific record is confined to the March 2021 death in Cheongju and its aftermath; no more recent provincial incident, enforcement action or policy change is recorded.
